newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Norway Christiania, Storebrand merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Norway Christiania, Storebrand merger.

text.p: Norway's Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and the country's leading insurer, Storebrand ASA, announced plans to merge on Wednesday to form the largest financial group in Norway and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.

The new company, Christiania Group, would have a market capitalisation of 26 billion crowns -- based on share prices at the close of business on March 26 -- and be the second largest listed company on the Oslo Stock exchange after industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA.
"The merger is the next logical step in the development of the two groups, which have both followed a strategy of providing a broad range of financial services," a joint statement said.

"The merged group will be able to play a more active role in a developing Nordic market and be better positioned for profitable growth than if each of the two groups were to remain separate," it said.

Each set of shareholders will hold 50 percent of the combined Christiania group. The agreed exchange ratio is based on market values with two ordinary shares in Christiania Bank equivalent to one ordinary Storebrand share.
The companies said they hoped to complete the deal by year end following government approval.
Storebrand's share was up four percent at 47.30 crowns at 1217 GMT. Christiania had risen two percent to 24.60 crowns.

"The merger is very exciting in terms of benefits both on the costs and revenues side," insurance analyst Nils Ringdal at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London told Reuters. "We see benefits of between 15 to 25 percent in terms of increased pre-tax profits in a few years say in 2000 or 2001."

The companies said the Christiania Bank and Storebrand brands would be retained and the principal elements of the two groups' operating structures -- banking, non-life insurance, life insurance/pensions and asset management -- would continue.

The merged Christiania will have a combined market share of 32 percent in the life insurance sector, five percentage points higher than Storebrand's current position, when Christiania Bank insurance division Norske Liv's market share is included.

In non-life insurance, the new group will have 39 percent of the market, while it will hold a market share of about 12 percent in traditional banking products, equal to Chrisitiania Bank's current position.

Aage Korsvold, chief executive officer at Storebrand and proposed CEO of the Christiania, said the company may look to expand in the Nordic market althought there were no concrete plans on an all-Nordic basis or at home.
"The most important competitors in our home market are our Nordic competitors," Korsvold told a news conference.
"It does not mean we are going to start a big wave of acquisitions outside Norway. But it may be that we should intensify our efforts in the other Nordic countries," he said.
Norway's overcrowded banking sector has been undergoing consolidation since the late 1980s and further mergers had been expected in the battle for market share amid slimmer margins.

DnB took over the country's second largest life insurer Vital Forsikring in January 1996, and entered into a bidding war on March 21 with Fokus Bank ASA for niche mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) BNKB.OL.
Analysts said the Christiania/Storebrand deal had left DnB in a difficult position.
"DnB is now in a strategic dilemma after today's announcement. I can't see how they can respond to this, they are out of options in the Norwegian market," said Ringdal .
Matthew Czepliewicz at Saloman Brothers said both Fokus Bank and DnB would be forced to rethink strategy.

"It puts Fokus bank in a rather awkward position. Suddenly they looked dwarfed by the consolidation that has already occurred at DnB with Vital and now is occurring at Christiania with Storebrand," Czepliewicz told Reuters Financial Television.

"It also turns the spotlight back on DnB itself, which prior to this had been the largest financial institution in the country. You have to ask whether DnB might not be interested in acquiring both BNbank and Fokus Bank," he said.
